name: QTS Data Centers (QTS Realty Trust, LLC)
founded: Founded by Chad Williams out of his family's Quality Group of Companies (Overland Park, Kansas; the company cites a 20+ year history); NYSE-listed as QTS Realty Trust 2013-2021; taken private by Blackstone August 2021
ownership: private (Blackstone — acquired 31 August 2021 for ~$10B including debt by Blackstone Infrastructure Partners, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and Blackstone Property Partners perpetual-capital vehicles)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: QTS is Blackstone's flagship AI-infrastructure asset — taken private in August 2021 for approximately $10B and grown since into what the company's own March 2025 release calls a '$60 billion global industry leader': leased capacity up 14x since the acquisition, 2GW of critical power operating as of March 2025 (3GW+ across 70+ facilities per 2026 trade rankings) and a $30B+ development pipeline pre-leased to investment-grade technology companies on 15-20-year escalating leases, per BREIT's FY2025 annual report. The growth machine is a standardized 'Freedom' building (36-72MW each) stamped across roughly two dozen US mega-campus sites — Fayetteville, GA (13 buildings, ~6.2M sq ft, housing at least one Microsoft AI 'superfactory' per trade press) is the flagship — funded by the sector's fastest securitization cadence and capped by an April 2026 $4.6B green bond that drew $12.5B of peak demand at QTS's first investment-grade rating (Baa2). Founder Chad Williams stepped down in April 2025; co-CEOs Tag Greason and David Robey now run the company. BACKGROUND: Built from Overland Park, Kansas colocation roots into a wholesale REIT (NYSE: QTS, 2013), the company was acquired at $78.00/share by Blackstone Infrastructure Partners, BREIT and Blackstone Property Partners, closing 31 August 2021. US headquarters is now Sterling, Virginia — a 77,000 sq ft Reston Station headquarters lease was signed August 2026 for ~2027 occupancy, with Overland Park operations retained — plus a London office. Europe: two operational Dutch sites (Eemshaven 20MW, Groningen 4MW), the £10B Cambois campus under construction in Northumberland, UK (approved at up to 720MW IT — repeatedly cited as the UK's largest AI data-centre project), and sites in consideration in Spain, Finland and Italy. The company rebranded its web presence to Q.com in March 2026. Expansion is meeting organized local resistance: QTS withdrew a $12B Dane County, Wisconsin campus in January 2026 after the Village of DeForest moved to reject annexation, and the Fayetteville campus drew a July 2026 water-use records controversy (county attributes ~29-30M unbilled gallons to a missed meter during a smart-meter transition; QTS paid at double construction rates once billed). Collection gap: no revenue or EBITDA has been disclosed since the take-private; the final public-year revenue was ~$540M (FY2020).
ecosystemRole: We assess QTS as the highest-velocity wholesale developer-landlord in this ecosystem and the single most consequential private account for US data-center supply chains in the Southeast and Midwest. Basis: Blackstone's BREIT filings ($30B+ pre-leased development pipeline, leased capacity up 14x since 2021, QTS at 20.4% of BREIT's real-estate value), the sector's fastest securitization pace per GlobalCapital, and a 2025-26 announcement run-rate of one new $10B-class campus roughly every other month (Cedar Rapids, Dane County, Van Wert, Hall County, Bessemer, Blakely). For power-chain, construction and cooling vendors the leverage point is the Freedom design: one standardized 36-72MW water-free building specification, replicated across every greenfield site and procured through repeat GC relationships (HITT — 7M+ sq ft delivered together per company claims — plus Gilbane and Layton on current campuses). We further assess the community-relations package — funding 100% of energy infrastructure, zero-water cooling, per-campus betterment funds — as a deliberate de-risking product aimed at the industry's binding constraint, local consent. Basis: near-identical commitment language across six 2025-26 campus announcements, the DeForest withdrawal, and the co-CEOs' public positioning.

productsAndServices.name: Hyperscale build-to-suit & wholesale mega-campuses (core business)
productsAndServices.description: Build-own-operate campuses leased wholesale to hyperscalers and AI platforms across ~45 named US sites plus Europe. Operational anchors (per q.com location pages): Atlanta 1 (278MW+, 99 acres), Richmond 1 (240MW+, 100 acres, the former Qimonda fab), Manassas (190MW+, 105 acres), Hillsboro 2 (180MW+), Irving, TX (165MW+), Denver/Aurora (160MW+), Chicago (95MW+), San Antonio (90MW+), three Ashburn campuses (55/75/80MW+), Fort Worth and East Windsor (70MW+ each), Piscataway (65MW+), Suwanee (50MW+). The development book is the story: Fayetteville, GA (13 buildings, ~6.2M sq ft, up to 16 at buildout — plus an ATL2 East filing for ~2M sq ft on ~313 acres), Cedar Rapids, IA ($10B, 612 acres, 7 buildings), Bessemer, AL ('Project Marvel' — up to 1.2GW, 18 buildings, 1,600 acres, $14.5B initial), Blakely, GA (1,400MW planned — the largest planned data center in Georgia per state project trackers), Hall County, TX with Lancium ($10B+), Van Wert, OH ($10B), South Dallas/Wilmer (DC1-DC3, ~118MW of filed critical capacity), Eagle Mountain, UT, two New Albany, OH sites, Richmond 2/3/5, Phoenix 2-4, Hillsboro 3, Augusta, GA and York County, SC — with Clinton, IA, Howard County, TX and Salem Township, PA in consideration.
highlights: Leased capacity up 14x since the 2021 take-private; $30B+ development pipeline pre-leased on 15-20-year leases with contractual escalators (BREIT FY2025 annual report)
Richmond RIC5 became the first data center ever covered by the federal FAST-41 permitting program (April 2026)
Fayetteville houses at least one Microsoft 'AI superfactory' building per trade reporting; Bloomberg tied the April 2026 bond collateral to Microsoft leases
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Vantage, Aligned, STACK and CloudHQ, QTS pairs what Blackstone calls one of the largest data-center pipelines in the world with a 3,000+ acre power-ready land bank and an in-house construction-management organization billed as among North America's largest; unlike public REITs Digital Realty and Equinix, perpetual private capital lets it buy land and power years ahead of leases. Site Selection Group (2026) ranks it the largest independent US operator at 70+ facilities / 3GW+.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct long-term wholesale and build-to-suit leases (15-20 years, escalators) with hyperscalers; campus debt recycled through ABS/CMBS securitizations and, since April 2026, investment-grade green bonds.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers (Microsoft linked by Bloomberg to Fayetteville collateral; other tenants unnamed)
productsAndServices.roadmap: South Dallas DC2 completes ~June 2026 and DC3 ~January 2027 per filings; Blakely pre-construction community payments run December 2026 onward with construction to follow; Bessemer, Hall County and Van Wert in entitlement; Dane County campus abandoned January 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Federal & government colocation
productsAndServices.description: A dedicated federal business built on purpose-built, federal-only data centers using a 'Federal Freedom Design' — the standard building adapted to government security and operational requirements — sited with geographic separation and multiple energy grids. Staffed by a federal assurance team of former government accrediting officials and security directors; 20%+ of the US workforce are veterans. The company advertises facilities built 'to safeguard sensitive and classified information' but names no agency customers; compliance documentation (SOC 2 Type 2 and other audited certifications) is delivered to customers through the SDP dashboard, and QTS has historically pursued FedRAMP readiness.
highlights: One of the few wholesale developers with a productized federal offering rather than ad-hoc government deals
Northern Virginia (Ashburn x3, Manassas) and Richmond concentration sits adjacent to federal demand
Named a Top Veteran Employer 2026 by US Veterans Magazine
productsAndServices.positioning: Versus Vantage/Aligned/STACK (no dedicated federal product) and Equinix (retail federal via interconnection), QTS sells federal isolation at wholesale scale; the trade-off is opacity — no public certification inventory or customer names, which we assess reflects classified-adjacent work rather than absence of it (analytic judgment, low confidence).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct with agencies and through federal cloud and systems-integrator intermediaries (company does not disclose the mix).
targetSegments: US federal civilian and defense agencies
productsAndServices.roadmap: None disclosed. Collection gap: QTS publishes no federal pipeline, certification roadmap or contract vehicle details.

productsAndServices.name: Enterprise colocation & connectivity
productsAndServices.description: The heritage retail/enterprise colocation business across the operational fleet — data halls, cages and cabinets with carrier-neutral meet-me rooms — now wrapped in a software-defined connectivity layer: the Switchboard SDN fabric, powered by Lumen as premier NaaS/SDN provider under an October 2025 partnership that also puts high-capacity (400G+) diverse fiber routes across 16 new QTS campuses in Arizona, Georgia, Ohio, Texas, Virginia and Oregon, deploys Lumen Connectivity Fabric into QTS multi-tenant environments, and rides Lumen's 340,000-route-mile backbone. In Europe, Zayo Europe was contracted (March 2026) to deliver network infrastructure for the Cambois campus.
highlights: Lumen deal covers automated connectivity to clouds, data centers and edge from inside QTS halls
Enterprise colocation is the legacy layer that maintains ecosystem credibility while wholesale drives growth
1,000+ customers historically claimed across the fleet
productsAndServices.positioning: QTS does not compete with Equinix/Digital Realty on internet-exchange density; it competes on campus-scale interconnection plus SDP transparency, and buys backbone reach through partners rather than owning fiber.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct enterprise sales and channel; services ordered and managed through the Service Delivery Platform.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Lumen fiber reaches the 16 new campuses as they energize (from 2026); no further connectivity roadmap disclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Freedom design platform (the standardized building product)
productsAndServices.description: QTS's productized data center: a standardized greenfield building specification — 36MW to 72MW of critical capacity per building, 285,000-570,000 sq ft gross, two to three stories, four or more data halls, power density up to 350W/sq ft — that standardizes architecture, critical equipment and logistics so builds are repeatable and fast ('quickest speed-to-market in the industry', company claim). Cooling is the differentiator: a low-pressure pumped-refrigerant, water-free system with indirect-air economization that consumes zero water for operational cooling — the company claims 48M+ gallons saved annually per data center and bills itself the global leader in water-free cooling. Liquid cooling for AI densities is integrated flexibly ('deployment-timing and methodology flexible'). A Federal Freedom variant layers on government security requirements; Cambois exports the design as ten three-story ~54,000 sqm halls of ~72MW each.
highlights: The basis of all new greenfield builds — one SKU replicated across every campus
Zero-water cooling is aimed squarely at the sector's #1 community objection
Designed to LEED standards with ENERGY STAR certification pursued; FSC wood, low-VOC materials, EV charging standard
productsAndServices.positioning: The direct analogue to Vantage's global blueprint and Aligned's Delta³ — QTS's differentiation is making water-free operation the fleet-wide default rather than a market-by-market option, which doubles as its permitting and community-consent argument.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold externally — the internal delivery vehicle for every QTS build-to-suit and speculative building.
targetSegments: Hyperscale build-to-suit customers who inherit the specification
productsAndServices.roadmap: Higher-density liquid-cooled variants for AI workloads per company statements; no dated public specification. Collection gap: QTS publishes no PUE/WUE fleet figures.

productsAndServices.name: Service Delivery Platform (SDP) software
productsAndServices.description: An API-driven orchestration and visibility platform the company calls the industry's first fully digitized data-center service layer: RESTful APIs and real-time applications aggregating power, connectivity, security-access and environment data into self-service dashboards ('360° digital control'). Additions over time: the 'Smart Family' of AI/ML remote-management tools (2021), an updated API-driven dashboard, and 'Intelligent Applications' (February 2023) including QTS Live Power (live raw power data to the sub-minute level) and a customer-tailored sustainability dashboard. Compliance documents (SOC 2 Type 2 and other audits) are served through the SDP Compliance Widget.
highlights: Sub-minute live power telemetry exposed directly to customers — unusual transparency for a wholesale landlord
Sustainability dashboard gives tenants per-deployment energy/carbon data for their own ESG reporting
Claims to be among the first providers to completely digitize systems and physical environments
productsAndServices.positioning: Versus Equinix Fabric (network-centric marketplace), SDP is facility-data-centric — the sales pitch is operational transparency and API access rather than ecosystem density. We assess it functions primarily as a retention/differentiation layer for enterprise and federal tenants rather than a revenue line (analytic judgment).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with colocation and wholesale contracts; not sold standalone.
productsAndServices.roadmap: None disclosed since the 2023 Intelligent Apps release. Collection gap: no public SDP roadmap under Blackstone ownership.

productsAndServices.name: Capital-markets & energy franchise
productsAndServices.description: The funding engine behind the pipeline. Securitization: no data-center issuer has matched QTS's pace in the public 144A market over the past two years (GlobalCapital) — ~$600M Phoenix ABS (September 2025; single 36MW hyperscale-tenant building, S&P A-), a $1.5B CMBS on Atlanta/Richmond facilities (2025), the record $3.46B CMBS (November 2025 — the largest data-center securitization of 2025, refinancing 10 stabilized data centers across six markets including Atlanta, Dallas and Norfolk), a $750M ABS (January 2026), a $1.95B CMBS (February 2026), and the April 2026 $4.6B green bond — a 10-year 5.700% deal maturing 2036, rated Baa2 by Moody's (QTS's first investment-grade corporate-style rating), drawing ~$12.5B of peak demand to fund two Fayetteville buildings. Energy: a Chief Energy Strategy Officer hire (2025), an Alliant Energy partnership to enable 750MW of new Wisconsin renewable generation (October 2025), an ENGIE/ABEI Lubio Solar PPA (48MWac of a 61MWac Kaufman County, TX project serving Irving operations, August 2026), a 120MWac Oregon solar build with Avangrid, PGE and Meta (December 2024), and a stated policy of funding 100% of the energy infrastructure its campuses require.
highlights: From ABS/CMBS to investment-grade project-style bonds in one cycle — the full capital stack now open
'We pay 100% of our energy costs' is deployed as both policy and marketing (Ratepayer-protection positioning)
AEP Ohio bill-assistance funding joined with other data-center developers (August 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: Vantage invented the data-center ABS; QTS is the current volume leader in issuance cadence, and Blackstone sponsorship gives it simultaneous access to ABS, CMBS and IG bond markets that few private developers can match. On power, QTS is utility-first (Alliant, AEP, Dominion, Georgia Power relationships) rather than microgrid-first like Vantage/Crusoe — the Lancium partnership is its first campus where a power developer owns the site.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 144A securitized notes, single-borrower CMBS, investment-grade green bonds; renewable PPAs executed with utilities and IPPs (ENGIE as intermediary).
productsAndServices.roadmap: The April 2026 green bond was described as the start of a ~$4.6B raise program (DCD); further issues expected as campuses stabilize.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENGIE-QTS PPA on ABEI Energy's Lubio Solar project (Kaufman County, TX): QTS takes 48MWac of the ~61MWac plant — ~150GWh/year — with ENGIE bundling retail supply and energy management for the Irving, TX data center operations
recentDevelopments.read: Texas renewables procurement keeps pace with the Dallas-area build-out — QTS keeps buying project-tied additionality rather than unbundled RECs.

recentDevelopments.headline: Blakely/Early County, GA community-investment framework disclosed: $7.5M/year for three years starting December 2026 (pre-construction), $4.5-12.5M per building per year once operational (projected $60-85M/year across the campus), and a $28.75M+ Community Betterment Fund
recentDevelopments.read: The consent playbook priced publicly for the first time — QTS pre-pays at campus scale for a site trackers list at 1,400MW, the largest planned data center in Georgia.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS signs a 77,000 sq ft lease at Reston Station (floors 11-13, 1800 Reston Row Plaza) to establish its headquarters, with occupancy ~mid-2027; Sterling and Overland Park operations are retained
recentDevelopments.read: The center of gravity formally moves to Data Center Alley two decades after the Overland Park founding — both co-CEOs already live in Virginia.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS and Lancium announce a $10B+ data center campus in Hall County, TX (near Turkey): QTS designs, builds and operates the buildings while Lancium owns the campus and delivers power via solar and battery resources; up to 7,000 construction jobs at peak, ~350 permanent
recentDevelopments.read: The first QTS campus where a power developer holds the land — time-to-power now shapes deal structure itself, not just siting.

recentDevelopments.headline: Records investigations report the Fayetteville, GA campus drew ~29-30M gallons over ~15 months before being billed; Fayette County attributes it to a missed meter reading during a smart-meter transition, bills QTS at the double-rate construction tariff, and QTS pays promptly — usage now <1% of county daily capacity
recentDevelopments.read: The zero-water marketing meets a metering scandal — the resolution favored QTS factually, but 'secretly guzzled 30 million gallons' headlines are the reputational price of being the biggest campus in the county.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS confirms it is behind 'Project Marvel' in Bessemer, AL: an initial $14.5B, 18-building campus on 700 acres, expanded by filing to ~1,600 acres and up to 1.2GW; land assembled in deals worth $870M+
recentDevelopments.read: A gigawatt-class campus assembled semi-anonymously before confirmation — the land-banking machine runs well ahead of disclosure.

recentDevelopments.headline: City of Van Wert, OH and QTS announce a $10B campus: AEP power with QTS funding 100% of energy infrastructure improvements, closed-loop water-free cooling, 1,500+ construction and ~200 permanent jobs, ~$200M of tax revenue over 20 years, plus a community betterment fund
recentDevelopments.read: The Midwest small-town template refined post-DeForest: utility named, ratepayer protection pledged and betterment fund attached on day one.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS launches a $4.6B green bond — 10-year, 5.700%, maturing 2036 — rated Baa2 by Moody's (its first investment-grade rating), drawing ~$12.5B of peak demand; proceeds fund/refinance two Fayetteville buildings, with Bloomberg tying the collateral to Microsoft
recentDevelopments.read: The IG debut: QTS graduates from ABS/CMBS takeouts to corporate-style project finance, and the order book priced AI-landlord risk at 5.7%.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS Richmond Technology Park Data Center 5 (RIC5) becomes the first data center ever granted federal FAST-41 permitting coverage, following the executive order on accelerating federal permitting of data-center infrastructure
recentDevelopments.read: Washington's pro-AI permitting doctrine lands on a QTS project first — a federal tailwind arriving exactly where local headwinds blow hardest.

recentDevelopments.headline: Zayo Europe contracted to deliver network infrastructure for the Cambois campus in Northumberland — billed as powering 'the UK's largest AI data centre' (approved at up to 720MW IT across ten halls)
recentDevelopments.read: The £10B UK bet gets its network spine while US Midwest siting fights flare — Europe remains the quieter half of the pipeline.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS rebrands its web presence to Q.com — a single-letter domain acquired from Quantum Fiber — and launches a national 'communities first' communications push emphasizing water-free cooling, self-funded energy infrastructure and local investment
recentDevelopments.read: Brand infrastructure for a company now arguing its case town by town — the marketing spend follows the consent constraint.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS withdraws its proposed $12B Dane County, WI campus after Village of DeForest staff recommend rejecting the ~1,600-acre annexation petition amid organized resident opposition; Dane County subsequently fast-tracks a data-center moratorium push
recentDevelopments.read: The first outright loss of a $10B-class site — proof the consent constraint binds even with $50M of commitments and 750MW of renewables attached.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS closes a $3.46B single-borrower CMBS — the largest data-center securitization of 2025 — refinancing 10 stabilized, hyperscale-leased data centers across six US markets including Atlanta, Dallas and Norfolk; follows a $1.5B CMBS on Atlanta/Richmond assets earlier in 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The buy-build-refinance flywheel at record scale: stabilized fleet recycles into cheap paper that funds the next tranche of campuses.

recentDevelopments.headline: QTS advances the Dane County, WI campus with a $50M community commitment (Madison College scholarships, UW research partnership, first-responder and nonprofit funding) and an Alliant Energy agreement to enable 750MW of new Wisconsin renewable generation
recentDevelopments.read: The consent package at maximum size — $50M plus 750MW of new renewables — and it still failed 90 days later: the ceiling on money-for-consent, found empirically.

recentDevelopments.headline: Lumen partnership: high-capacity (400G+) diverse fiber routes interconnecting 16 new QTS campuses across six states, Lumen as premier NaaS/SDN provider powering QTS's Switchboard fabric, and Lumen Connectivity Fabric deployed into QTS multi-tenant environments
recentDevelopments.read: Connectivity was the wholesale model's weak flank versus Equinix — QTS outsources the fix to Lumen's 340,000-route-mile backbone rather than building its own.

recentDevelopments.headline: Enabling works begin at the £10B Cambois campus (former Blyth Power Station site, Northumberland) with a Social Value Programme launch; planning was approved March 2025 for ten halls totaling up to 720MW IT / ~540,000 sqm
recentDevelopments.read: QTS's first ground-up European campus moves dirt — a decade of small Dutch sites gives way to the UK's largest data-centre project.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cedar Rapids, IA campus announced: $10B, 612 acres in the Big Cedar Industrial Center, 7 buildings, Alliant Energy carbon-free power partnership, ~4B gallons/year of water conserved versus evaporative designs, up to $18M into a city-owned Community Betterment Fund — called the largest investment in Iowa history
recentDevelopments.read: The Midwest pivot lands its anchor: cheap land, a willing utility, and water-free cooling deployed as the political wedge.

recentDevelopments.headline: Founder and CEO Chad Williams steps down (effective April 18) after 20+ years, returning to Quality Group of Companies; COO David Robey and Chief Growth Officer Tag Greason appointed co-CEOs — the release cites a '$60 billion global industry leader' with 1,600+ employees and 2GW of critical power
recentDevelopments.read: Founder exit at the top of the cycle — Blackstone installs an operator/seller duo, the standard PE succession for a platform this scaled.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess QTS is Blackstone's template for converting permanent capital into supply velocity — the platform most likely to set the market-clearing pace of US wholesale delivery. Basis: leased capacity up 14x since the 2021 take-private, a $30B+ pre-leased pipeline on 15–20-year investment-grade leases (BREIT FY2025), a 2025–26 cadence of one $10B-class campus announcement roughly every other month, and the sector's fastest securitization pace capped by the $4.6B Baa2 green bond (Apr 2026, $12.5B peak demand).

(High confidence) We assess the standardized Freedom building is the operating moat: one repeatable 36–72MW water-free product that turns vendor relationships into fleet-wide procurement. Basis: roughly two dozen US mega-campus sites stamped from a single design, water-free operation as the fleet default rather than a market-by-market option, in-house construction management, and a 3,000+ acre power-ready land bank feeding the machine.

(High confidence) We assess community consent — not power, land or capital — is now QTS's binding constraint. Basis: the Dane County/DeForest withdrawal (Jan 2026) despite a $50M community package and 750MW of new renewables — the first outright loss of a $10B-class site; the publicly priced Blakely consent framework ($7.5M/yr for three years); a national brand campaign (Q.com) built to argue the case town by town; with federal FAST-41 permitting (RIC5, Apr 2026) arriving as the countervailing tailwind.

(Moderate confidence) We assess deal structure is bending from land-first to power-first assembly. Basis: the Hall County, TX campus (Jul 2026) where power developer Lancium holds the land and QTS designs, builds and operates; Van Wert's structure with QTS funding 100% of AEP's energy-infrastructure improvements; and project-tied additionality PPAs (ENGIE/ABEI Lubio Solar) — time-to-power now shapes who owns what in the deal, not just where campuses land.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the founder-to-operators succession marks exit-track institutionalization rather than a strategy change. Basis: Chad Williams' April 2025 departure at the top of the cycle, the operator/seller co-CEO pairing (Greason/Robey), the headquarters move to Data Center Alley (Reston Station, Aug 2026), and the investment-grade ratings debut — the standard private-equity sequence for a platform being groomed for eventual monetization.

metrics.name: Take-private
metrics.actual: $78.00/share all-cash, ~$10B including debt — announced June 7, 2021; completed August 31, 2021 by Blackstone Infrastructure Partners, BREIT and Blackstone Property Partners (all perpetual-capital vehicles)
metrics.result: A 21% premium to the prior close at announcement; QTS was then a ~$540M-revenue REIT

metrics.name: Value mark
metrics.actual: 'A $60 billion global industry leader' — the company's own March 2025 CEO-transition release; roughly a 6x mark versus the $10B entry in under four years
metrics.result: Company/Blackstone characterization, not a market transaction

metrics.name: BREIT weighting
metrics.actual: QTS represents 20.4% of BREIT's real-estate value per the FY2025 annual report; leased capacity up 14x since the 2021 acquisition
metrics.result: The single largest position in BREIT's portfolio

metrics.name: Platform context
metrics.actual: Blackstone's overall data-center business was internally valued at ~$185B at Q2 2026, up from ~$130B at the start of 2026 (earnings coverage) — a figure that includes QTS alongside other holdings
metrics.result: Schwarzman called data centers 'the largest development business in the world'

periods.commentary: Ownership split between Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT (with Blackstone Property Partners) is not disclosed in percentage terms. No QTS-specific standalone valuation has been marked publicly beyond the March 2025 '$60 billion' characterization.

metrics.name: Securitization cadence
metrics.actual: No public-144A data-center issuer has matched QTS's pace over the past two years (GlobalCapital): ~$600M Phoenix ABS (Sep 2025; single 36MW hyperscale-leased building, S&P A-), $1.5B CMBS on Atlanta/Richmond assets (2025), record $3.46B CMBS (Nov 2025 — largest data-center securitization of 2025; 10 stabilized data centers across six markets), $750M ABS (Jan 2026), $1.95B CMBS (Feb 2026)
metrics.result: Stabilized, hyperscale-leased assets recycled into rated paper to fund the development pipeline

metrics.name: Green bond (IG debut)
metrics.actual: $4.6B, 10-year, 5.700% coupon, maturing 2036 — April 2026; first-time Baa2 rating from Moody's; ~$12.5B peak demand; issued by two subsidiaries tied to two Fayetteville, GA buildings, with Bloomberg reporting the collateral is Microsoft-leased
metrics.result: Opens the investment-grade market on top of ABS/CMBS; described by DCD as the start of a ~$4.6B raise program

metrics.name: Development funding base
metrics.actual: $30B+ development pipeline pre-leased to large, investment-grade global technology companies on 15-20-year leases with contractual rent escalators (BREIT FY2025 annual report)
metrics.result: Pre-leasing is the credit story: construction risk with contracted takeout

periods.commentary: Collection gap: aggregate program size, leverage and cost-of-debt figures are not disclosed — the deal list above is assembled from ratings coverage and trade press, not any company capital-markets summary.

metrics.name: Capacity
metrics.actual: 2GW of critical power operating and 1,600+ employees (company release, March 2025); 3GW+ across 70+ facilities per Site Selection Group's 2026 ranking — the largest independent US data-center operator
metrics.result: Company disclosures stopped at the March 2025 release; third-party trackers carry the 2026 figures

metrics.name: Land bank
metrics.actual: 3,000+ acres of power-ready sites (company hyperscale page); ~45 named US locations plus 6 European sites as of August 2026
metrics.result: Land/power banking years ahead of leases is the stated strategy

metrics.name: Last public financials
metrics.actual: ~$540M revenue in FY2020, the final full year as a public REIT (trade-press context at the take-private)
metrics.result: Illustrates the scale multiple since: leased capacity 14x, valuation ~6x

periods.commentary: Collection gap: QTS has disclosed no revenue, EBITDA, leverage or consolidated balance-sheet figures since going private in 2021, and no analyst consensus exists — every 'expected' field is left empty rather than reconstructed. Employee count (1,600+) is stale as of March 2025. Tenant names are never confirmed by the company; the Microsoft association rests on Bloomberg and trade reporting.

financials.commentary: Collection gap: QTS has published no revenue, EBITDA, leverage or balance-sheet figures since the August 2021 take-private. Scale must be read through sponsor disclosures (BREIT annual reports, Blackstone earnings commentary), securitization collateral data and rating-agency reports; the '$60B industry leader' and '14x leased capacity' figures are company/sponsor-attributed and independently unverified. No analyst consensus exists for any period — every 'expected' field is left empty rather than reconstructed.
